instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Corporate law firm with 45 lawyers specializing in M&A, tax structuring, competition law, and cross-border transactions. Serving 200+ corporate clients across technology, financial services, and energy sectors. Evaluating AI-assisted contract review and due diligence document analysis tools.
answers.pastInitiatives: Our engineering team adopted an agile methodology last year, moving from waterfall-style quarterly releases to 2-week sprints with continuous deployment. This reduced our release cycle time by 60% and improved cross-functional collaboration. However, adjacent teams (marketing, support) are still adapting to the faster cadence.
answers.strategicGoals: The board has challenged us to improve EBITDA margins by 500 basis points within 3 years. This requires a disciplined, data-driven approach to identifying cost drivers and process bottlenecks. We are open to technology investment if it demonstrably reduces unit costs or eliminates manual touchpoints, but every project must have a clear ROI timeline of under 12 months.
answers.teamSize: Innovation is decentralized across business units, each with its own innovation lead and dedicated resources, coordinated by a group-level Chief Innovation Officer. The total innovation workforce is approximately 100 people across the organization.
answers.additionalContext: The legal tech landscape is rapidly shifting towards generative AI, presenting both an opportunity for radical process overhaul and significant talent acquisition challenges.

opportunities.title: Generative AI Integration in Automated Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)
opportunities.rationale: Implementing a generative AI tool to automatically review M&A agreements and due diligence documents can drastically reduce the 80% of time currently spent on manual document review, directly impacting operational efficiency. Given our bold risk appetite, investing heavily in this technology now could create a significant competitive moat.

first_actions: Conduct a proof-of-concept (PoC) with the M&A practice group
Identify and secure specialized legal AI talent for pilot phase
Establish clear data governance protocols for proprietary client documents
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduce document review time per transaction by 70% within Q4
milestones: Full integration pilot in one business unit (Month 6)

opportunities.title: Optimized Internal Workflow Automation (RPA)
opportunities.rationale: Deploy Robotic Process Automation (RPA) tools to automate repetitive, high-volume administrative tasks like client onboarding document processing and fee tracking. This provides immediate efficiency gains by eliminating manual touchpoints without requiring major foundational system overhauls.

first_actions: Audit the top 5 most time-consuming back-office workflows
Select an RPA platform vendor (e.g., UiPath)
Map out automation routes for immediate process gains
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve a 25% reduction in administrative processing costs within the year
milestones: Phase 1 RPA deployment completion and KPI tracking (Month 4)

next_steps.action: Appoint a cross-functional steering committee to prioritize the AI PoC roadmap.
Develop detailed budget scenarios for both radical and incremental efficiency projects.
Begin scouting legal AI talent pools to address the core 'talent' barrier.

key_weaknesses: Inconsistent innovation process across decentralized business units, leading to fragmented adoption.
Budgetary constraints limiting the scope and scale of long-term radical investments despite a bold appetite for risk.
Critical talent gap in specialized AI/Legal tech expertise necessary to execute high-impact efficiency initiatives.
